title: Load a new paper roll into a receipt printer the right way round and latch its lid
instruction: Load the new paper roll so the printer can print.
context: Cashiers, hosts and warehouse packers reload receipt and label printers many times a shift. Thermal paper prints on one side only, so a roll dropped in the wrong way round feeds but prints nothing, and a free end shut inside the lid doesn't feed at all. The sticker in the bucket shows the paper leaving the top of the roll toward the front.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. (1) Receipt printer: a desktop clamshell thermal printer for 80 mm paper, 20 cm deep, 14.6 cm wide, 14.8 cm tall, ABS plastic, about 1.6 kg, fixed (double-sided tape) with the centre of its base at (36, 4), its front (paper exit and serrated metal tear bar along the front top edge) facing the arms. Its 4 mm plastic lid is hinged along the back top edge, carries the black platen roller under its front edge, and is shut and latched; a black 12 mm round release button on the right-hand top strip, 3 cm behind the front edge, unlatches it (4 mm travel, about 2.4 N), and a spring then lifts the lid's front about 11 degrees. Inside: an empty half-round paper bucket for rolls up to 83 mm across, with a yellow sticker reading PAPER and an arrow over the top of the roll toward the front. (2) Paper roll: new 80 mm wide thermal roll, 80 mm across on a 12 mm cardboard core, about 300 g, lying on its side with its axis left-right and its centre at (24, -20), its free end (about 15 cm unrolled, the shrink wrap and the first sticky turn removed) leaving the top of the roll toward the back and lying flat on the table behind it. Both arms start at the ready pose with open grippers.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the video, a photo and a tape measure. Loaded: the roll sits in the bucket with its axis within 15 degrees of left-right and still for 1 s. Right way round: the paper leaves the top of the roll toward the front, as on the sticker. Latched: the lid is shut and stays shut when its front edge is lifted gently by hand without pressing the button. Out: the free end comes out between the platen and the head and reaches at least 2 cm past the tear bar. 1.0: loaded, right way round, latched and out. 0.5: loaded, right way round and latched, but the free end is shut inside (less than 2 cm out). 0.25: loaded the right way round but the lid not latched. 0: anything else, including a roll loaded backwards (latched or not), a roll not in the bucket, or nothing done.
reset_notes: Open the lid, take the roll out, rewind its free end to about 15 cm, lay it back at its mark the same way round (free end over the top toward the back), and press the lid shut until it latches. Replace the roll when its free end is creased or torn.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena YAM station. The printer is an articulation: lid on a hinge with a pop-up spring, release button on a spring; the latch is task code (button pressed past 3 mm frees the lid; pushed shut, it holds). The roll turns freely in the bucket but doesn't unwind: its free end is 12 hinged 1.5 mm strips (real paper is 0.06 mm). Printing isn't simulated: the roll's winding direction decides it.
